question: Does impure feed or mistreatment of animals make their meat haram?
answer:
Then there's one other issue that comes, and a lot of people say: how about the feed of the animal? You're feeding them najis. Remember mad cow disease, bovine disease, a decade ago, when they discovered that they're feeding animals to animals? The najis aspects of the slaughterhouses: they're sacrificing pigs and cows in the same slaughterhouses.

All of these things are definitely makruh; they should be avoided. But they're nowhere near as big as the first three factors, so don't make the meat haram just based upon that. Genetically modified, or GMO, or what you're feeding them, all of these things, unethical treatment: all of this is something that is makruh, but it doesn't make the animal haram. There is a sin on the farmer who mistreats the cow, but when the cow is slaughtered properly, it doesn't make it haram for us. Now, if you choose to not buy such a product, fine for you, but don't make it haram for the rest of the world. If you want to raise your own bar, good for you, but don't bring in Islamic law and make it haram.

When it comes to haram and halal, we look at a number of factors. When it comes to adab and etiquette, we look at other factors. And we can say the unethical treatment of animals is sinful for the farmer. We can say it is very, very clear that somebody who mistreats an animal might end up in Jahannam, like the one who mistreated the cat and she ended up in Jahannam. Very clear. But if an animal is mistreated, and then it is slaughtered in a proper manner, the final result of the meat does not make it haram. Now, you can choose ethically to say, "I don't want to do that," and that's totally fine. But, like I said, don't make it haram on the rest of the world, who maybe can't afford to have the standards that you can have.
